title: Rigveda 1.21: To Indra and Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.21: To Indra and Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.21 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Indra and Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 10v-11r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.21.1-3 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 2, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 10v
translation.original_text:
1i̱hendrā̱gnī upa̍ hvaye̱ tayo̱r it stoma̍m uśmasi | tā soma̍ṁ soma̱pāta̍mā ||
2tā ya̱jñeṣu̱ pra śa̍ṁsatendrā̱gnī śu̍mbhatā naraḥ | tā gā̍ya̱treṣu̍ gāyata ||
3tā mi̱trasya̱ praśa̍staya indrā̱gnī tā ha̍vāmahe | so̱ma̱pā soma̍pītaye ||
translation.text:
1INDRA and Agni I invoke fain are we for their song of praise Chief Soma-drinkers are they both.
2Praise ye, O men, and glorify Indra-Agni in the holy rites: Sing praise to them in sacred songs.
3Indra and Agni we invite, the Soma-drinkers, for the fame Of Mitra, to the Soma-draught.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 10v (OPenn image 12, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.20.1 ‹-akāri ratna-dhātamaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 11r, begins in RV 1.21.4 ‹upa idam savanam sutam›. Verses 1.21.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1iha | indrāgnī iti | upa | hvaye | tayoḥ | it | stomam | uśmasi | tā | somam | soma-pātamā
2tā | yajñeṣu | pra | śaṃsata | indrāgnī iti | śumbhata | naraḥ | tā | gāyatreṣu | gāyata
3tā | mitrasya | pra-śastaye | indrāgnī iti | tā | havāmahe | soma-pā | soma-pītaye

translation.original_ref: RV 1.21.4-6 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 2, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 11r
translation.original_text:
4u̱grā santā̍ havāmaha̱ upe̱daṁ sava̍naṁ su̱tam | i̱ndrā̱gnī eha ga̍cchatām ||
5tā ma̱hāntā̱ sada̱spatī̱ indrā̍gnī̱ rakṣa̍ ubjatam | apra̍jāḥ santv a̱triṇa̍ḥ ||
6tena̍ sa̱tyena̍ jāgṛta̱m adhi̍ prace̱tune̍ pa̱de | indrā̍gnī̱ śarma̍ yacchatam ||
translation.text:
4Strong Gods, we bid them come to this libation that stands ready here: Indra and Agni, come to us.
5Indra and Agni, mighty Lords of our assembly, crush the fiends: Childless be the devouring ones.
6Watch ye, through this your truthfulness, there in the place of spacious view Indra and Agni, send us bliss.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 11r (OPenn image 12, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.21.4 ‹upa idam savanam sutam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 11v, begins in RV 1.22.10 ‹agne iha avase hotrām›. Verses 1.21.4-6 end on this page; 1.21.4 begins on fol. 10v.
translation.edition_text:
4ugrā | santā | havāmahe | upa | idam | savanam | sutam | indrāgnī iti | ā | iha | gacchatām
5tā | mahāntā | sadaspatī iti | indrāgnī iti | rakṣaḥ | ubjatam | aprajāḥ | santu | atriṇaḥ
6tena | satyena | jāgṛtam | adhi | pra-cetune | pade | indrāgnī iti | śarma | yacchatam
